headline: Profit rebounds sharply after a disrupted first quarter
summary_short: ExxonMobil earned $14.5B ($3.48 diluted EPS) in Q2 2026, up sharply q/q from $4.2B in Q1 as Energy Products swung to a $5.5B profit from a $1.3B loss.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $114.5B, up 34.5% q/q and 40.5% y/y, as Upstream earnings climbed to $7.9B on record Permian output above 1.8 million boe/d and Energy Products swung to a $5.5B profit from a $1.3B loss on strong Gulf Coast refining utilization. Chemical and Specialty Products earnings also improved. Operating cash flow was $23.6B and free cash flow $17.2B, funding $9.4B of shareholder distributions ($4.3B dividends, $5.1B buybacks) while YTD capex held at $13.0B and cumulative structural cost savings reached $16.3B versus 2019. Management gave no specific FY2026 earnings or production guidance, citing a portfolio built for varying market conditions rather than one quarter.

drivers.explanation: CEO Woods said the quarter was shaped by disruption but defined by execution, as Kazakhstan-related disruptions eased and integrated operations offset market volatility.
Energy Products swung to a $5.5B profit from a $1.3B loss quarter-over-quarter, the single largest driver of the net income recovery.
Upstream earnings rose to $7.9B from $5.7B on record Permian output above 1.8 million boe/d and the absence of Q1's Middle East-linked disruptions.
High U.S. Gulf Coast refining utilization and North American feedstock advantages supported product margins in Energy Products and Chemicals this quarter.
